intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency-2 (COQ10D2) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the PDSS1 gene on chromosome 10.

checks.claim: Primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency-2 (COQ10D2) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the PDSS1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: PDSS1 defect has been described in three patients from two families 6, 7 carrying three pathogenic variants in the PDSS1 gene, homozygous in one family and compound heterozygote in the other (Table 1).
checks.explanation: The paper describes homozygous and compound heterozygous PDSS1 variants causing CoQ10 deficiency.

checks.claim: The PDSS1 gene is located on chromosome 10.
checks.evidence_quote: A genome-wide search for homozygosity in family 1 identified a region of chromosome 10 encompassing the gene prenyldiphosphate synthase, subunit 1 (PDSS1)
checks.explanation: The abstract states that PDSS1 lies in the region it identified on chromosome 10.

paragraphs.text: Primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency-2 (COQ10D2) is an autosomal recessive disorder of CoQ10 biosynthesis that causes oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) deficiency (Mollet et al., 2007). The phenotype varies widely. Some patients have sensorineural deafness followed by optic atrophy, with mild intellectual disability, muscle weakness, and cardiac valvulopathy. Others have a severe infantile multisystem disorder that includes encephalopathy, nephrotic syndrome or pulmonary hypertension, and early death (Nardecchia et al., 2021; Bellusci et al., 2021).

checks.claim: COQ10D2 is an autosomal recessive disorder of CoQ10 biosynthesis.
checks.evidence_quote: We have identified 2 novel inborn errors of CoQ10 biosynthesis in 2 distinct families.
checks.explanation: The abstract supports an inborn error of CoQ10 biosynthesis, and its homozygous mutation fits recessive inheritance. It never states autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: COQ10D2 causes oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) deficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: indicating that these mutations are indeed the cause of OXPHOS deficiency
checks.explanation: The abstract says these mutations cause the OXPHOS deficiency.

checks.claim: The phenotype of COQ10D2 varies widely.
checks.evidence_quote: PDSS1 deficiency is a clinically heterogenous rare disorder that deserves to be added to the differential diagnosis of optic atrophy associated with sensorineural deafness.
checks.explanation: The paper calls the disorder clinically heterogeneous.

checks.claim: Some patients with COQ10D2 have sensorineural deafness followed by optic atrophy, with mild intellectual disability, muscle weakness, and cardiac valvulopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: was characterized by neurosensorial deafness, optic atrophy, mild intellectual disability, muscular weakness, and cardiac involvement consisting in mild to moderate valvulopathy. Notably, in these cases, neurosensorial loss preceded optic atrophy, like in our cases.
checks.explanation: The paper describes this phenotype in the Mollet siblings and in the present cases.

checks.claim: Some patients with COQ10D2 have a severe infantile multisystem disorder including encephalopathy, nephrotic syndrome or pulmonary hypertension, and early death.
checks.evidence_quote: a much severe phenotype characterized by leukoencephalopathy with a lactic acid peak on spectroscopy, associated with a severe nephrotic syndrome that caused kidney failure and death at the age of 16 months.
checks.explanation: The paper supports encephalopathy, nephrotic syndrome and early death, but it never mentions pulmonary hypertension.

paragraphs.text: Mollet et al. (2007) found an inborn error of CoQ10 biosynthesis in a family (family 1) with OXPHOS deficiency. Nardecchia et al. (2021) summarized the clinical features of this family's 2 affected sibs, a male examined at 22 years and a female examined at 14 years. Both had mild intellectual disability, lactic acidosis, macrocephaly, peripheral neuropathy, muscle weakness or exercise intolerance, sensorineural deafness, optic atrophy, and cardiac valvulopathy, as well as obesity/livedo reticularis. In both sibs, sensorineural hearing loss came before optic atrophy.

paragraphs.text: Nardecchia et al. (2021) reported 2 sisters with COQ10D2 born to consanguineous Egyptian parents. The proband was 16 years old at the time of the report. She had severe language delay, and profound bilateral sensorineural hearing loss was found at age 4 years. Mild intellectual disability was diagnosed later. Her visual acuity was normal at 11 years but had fallen to 1/10 bilaterally by 14 years, with red-green dyschromatopsia. Fundus examination showed optic atrophy that was most marked in the inferior temporal sector. Visual evoked potentials showed increased P100 latency and reduced amplitude, and optical coherence tomography showed reduced retinal nerve fiber layer thickness. She also had diffuse mild muscle weakness and a mild postural tremor of the upper limbs. Brain MRI was normal. Echocardiography showed a moderately dysplastic mitral valve with moderate insufficiency, tricuspid insufficiency, and a moderately dilated left atrium. Her 6-year-old sister had bilateral sensorineural hearing loss. At age 6 she developed decreased visual acuity, with optic atrophy and divergent strabismus. Neither sister had lactic acidosis.

paragraphs.text: Bellusci et al. (2021) reported a boy with COQ10D2 who was born prematurely. At age 5 months he had failure to thrive, hypotonia, feeding difficulties, bilateral hearing impairment, pulmonary hypertension, livedo reticularis, and chronic distal phalangeal erythema. Laboratory studies showed anemia, lactic acidosis, 3-methylglutaconic and tricarboxylic aciduria, and decreased CoQ10 levels in lymphocytes. He developed a progressive multisystem disorder with severe developmental delay, pyramidal dysfunction, seizures, tremor, optic atrophy, nystagmus, severe visual and hearing impairment, and chronic heart failure. Brain MRI showed mild cerebral atrophy at 12 months and cystic white matter changes at 24 months. High-dose CoQ10 supplementation did not halt progression, and he died at 3 years of age.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a family with CoQ10 deficiency (COQ10D2), Mollet et al. (2007) identified a homozygous mutation in the PDSS1 gene that results in an asp308-to-glu (D308E) substitution at a conserved residue. Nardecchia et al. (2021) gave the nucleotide change as c.924T-G. When the corresponding mutant yeast COQ1 gene was transformed into a yeast Delta-coq1 strain, the cells grew poorly on respiratory medium.

checks.claim: In affected members of a family with COQ10D2, Mollet et al. (2007) identified a homozygous PDSS1 mutation resulting in an asp308-to-glu (D308E) substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: Sequencing of PDSS1 identified a homozygous nucleotide substitution modifying a conserved amino acid of the protein (D308E).
checks.explanation: D308E is the same change as asp308-to-glu.

checks.claim: The PDSS1 D308E substitution occurs at a conserved residue.
checks.evidence_quote: modifying a conserved amino acid of the protein (D308E)
checks.explanation: The abstract states that the residue is conserved.

checks.claim: Nardecchia et al. (2021) gave the nucleotide change of PDSS1 D308E as c.924T-G.
checks.evidence_quote: c.924T> G (p.Asp308Glu) homozygous
checks.explanation: Table 1 gives the nucleotide change as c.924T>G.

checks.claim: Yeast Delta-coq1 cells transformed with the mutant yeast COQ1 gene corresponding to PDSS1 D308E grew poorly on respiratory medium.
checks.evidence_quote: Transformation of yeast Deltacoq1 and Deltacoq2 strains by mutant yeast COQ1 and mutant human COQ2 genes, respectively, resulted in defective growth on respiratory medium
checks.explanation: The abstract reports defective growth of the transformed Deltacoq1 strain on respiratory medium.

paragraphs.text: In 2 sisters with COQ10D2 born to consanguineous Egyptian parents, Nardecchia et al. (2021) identified a homozygous c.735G-T transversion in the PDSS1 gene that results in a gln245-to-his (Q245H) substitution at a highly conserved position. The mutation was found by whole-exome sequencing and was absent from gnomAD. Both parents were heterozygous. Of the 2 unaffected sibs, one was heterozygous and the other was homozygous wildtype.

checks.claim: In 2 sisters with COQ10D2 born to consanguineous Egyptian parents, Nardecchia et al. (2021) identified a homozygous c.735G-T transversion in the PDSS1 gene resulting in a gln245-to-his (Q245H) substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: A whole‐exome sequencing analysis revealed a homozygous likely pathogenic missense variant c.735G > T in the PDSS1 gene, never reported in the public database GnomAD. This variant causes the amino acid change p.Gln245His
checks.explanation: The variant and protein change match. The sister's homozygosity is also confirmed in the paper.

checks.claim: The PDSS1 Q245H substitution occurs at a highly conserved position.
checks.evidence_quote: This variant causes the amino acid change p.Gln245His, in a highly conserved position (98.5%, Fig. 1A).

checks.claim: The PDSS1 Q245H mutation was found by whole-exome sequencing.
checks.evidence_quote: A whole‐exome sequencing analysis revealed a homozygous likely pathogenic missense variant c.735G > T in the PDSS1 gene

checks.claim: The PDSS1 Q245H mutation was absent from gnomAD.
checks.evidence_quote: never reported in the public database GnomAD

checks.claim: Both parents of the Egyptian sisters were heterozygous for PDSS1 Q245H.
checks.evidence_quote: its segregation was confirmed in her parents (I:1 and I:2).
checks.explanation: Confirmed segregation of a homozygous variant in both parents means both are heterozygous carriers.

checks.claim: Of the 2 unaffected sibs of the Egyptian sisters, one was heterozygous for PDSS1 Q245H and the other was homozygous wildtype.
checks.evidence_quote: the unaffected sister (II:2) and brother (II:3) was, respectively, homozygous wild‐type and heterozygous for the variant

paragraphs.text: In a boy with severe COQ10D2 who died at age 3 years, Bellusci et al. (2021) identified compound heterozygous mutations in the PDSS1 gene. One was a c.716T-G transversion (NM_014317.3) that results in a val239-to-gly (V239G) substitution. The other was a c.1183C-T transition that results in an arg395-to-ter (R395X) substitution.

checks.claim: Bellusci et al. (2021) identified compound heterozygous PDSS1 mutations in a boy with severe COQ10D2 who died at age 3 years.
checks.evidence_quote: biallelic PDSS1 mutations were identified (NM_014317.3: c.716 T > G (p.Val239Gly) and NM_014317.3: c.1183C > T (p.Arg395*))
checks.explanation: Two different biallelic variants in a boy who died at 3 years.

checks.claim: One PDSS1 mutation in the boy reported by Bellusci et al. (2021) was a c.716T-G transversion (NM_014317.3) resulting in a val239-to-gly (V239G) substitution.
The other PDSS1 mutation in the boy reported by Bellusci et al. (2021) was a c.1183C-T transition resulting in an arg395-to-ter (R395X) substitution.

paragraphs.text: For discussion of the c.1183C-T transition (NM_014317.3) in the PDSS1 gene, which results in an arg395-to-ter (R395X) substitution and was found in compound heterozygous state in a patient with COQ10D2 by Bellusci et al. (2021), see the V239G entry.

checks.claim: The PDSS1 c.1183C-T transition (NM_014317.3) results in an arg395-to-ter (R395X) substitution.
Bellusci et al. (2021) found the PDSS1 R395X mutation in compound heterozygous state in a patient with COQ10D2.
checks.evidence_quote: biallelic PDSS1 mutations were identified (NM_014317.3: c.716 T > G (p.Val239Gly) and NM_014317.3: c.1183C > T (p.Arg395*))
checks.explanation: Found with V239G in biallelic (compound heterozygous) state.
